gloss: to inherit; to succeed to; to take over

definitions.explanation: To receive something (property, traditions, skills, etc.) from a predecessor and continue with it.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}から{家業|かぎょう}を{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ。
examples.english: I inherited the family business from my grandfather.

examples.japanese: この{伝統|でんとう}は{何世代|なんせだい}にもわたって{受|う}け{継|つ}がれてきた。
examples.english: This tradition has been passed down through many generations.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}の{料理|りょうり}の{腕|うで}を{受|う}け{継|つ}ぎたい。
examples.english: I want to inherit my mother's cooking skills.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ → {受|う}け{継|つ}がない (negative)
・{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ → {受|う}け{継|つ}いで (te-form)
・{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ → {受|う}け{継|つ}いだ (past)

FORMATION:
Compound verb: {受|う}ける (to receive) + {継|つ}ぐ (to succeed/inherit)

USAGE:
Often used in passive form {受|う}け{継|つ}がれる to describe traditions or qualities being passed down:
・{技術|ぎじゅつ}が{受|う}け{継|つ}がれる (skills are passed down)
・{意志|いし}を{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ (to carry on someone's will)
・{財産|ざいさん}を{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ (to inherit property)
・DNAを{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ (to inherit DNA/genes)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぐ - focuses on taking over duties/responsibilities
・{継|つ}ぐ - simpler form, to succeed/inherit
